learningObjective: Compute the KV cache memory footprint of a specific model configuration and reason about capacity limits.

canonicalClaims.claim: Per-token KV cache footprint = 2 (K and V) * L (layers) * H_kv * d * sizeof(dtype); total capacity = HBM budget for KV / per-token footprint.
conditions: H_kv is the number of KV heads (not query heads).
nonImplications: Does not account for paged-cache internal fragmentation.
Does not include workspace or activation buffers.

misconceptions.claim: Per-token KV uses H (query heads), not H_kv.
misconceptions.whyWrong: MQA/GQA is defined precisely to reduce this to H_kv; using H overstates the footprint.

misconceptions.claim: Per-token KV is one entry across all layers.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Every layer has its own KV cache; total is L * per-layer.

misconceptions.claim: KV cache is a fixed cost per sequence and does not scale with length.
misconceptions.whyWrong: KV grows one entry per token per layer.

implementationFacts: Per-token KV for Llama-2-7B (32L, 32 KV, 128 d, FP16) = 512 KB; Llama-2-70B GQA (80L, 8 KV, 128 d, FP16) = 320 KB.
KV cache is often the tightest resource for long-context batch serving.
performanceScenarios: Doubling context length cuts effective batch size roughly in half at fixed HBM budget.
MQA/GQA and KV quantization are direct capacity levers.
